title: Completed local ring of an etale chart at a rational point after field extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $U$ be a $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme] with an etale morphism $t=(t_1,\ldots,t_n):U\to\mathbf A^n_k$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] [def-sbc-affine-space] of $k$-schemes, $n\ge0$, let $L\supseteq k$ be a field extension, put $U_L=U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $b\in U_L$ be a point whose residue field $\kappa(b)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is $L$, i.e. the map $L\to\kappa(b)$ induced by the projection $U_L\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ is an isomorphism. Write $t_i$ also for its pullback to $U_L$, $c_i\in L$ for the value of $t_i$ at $b$ (its image in $\kappa(b)=L$), $\mathcal O_{U_L,b}$ for the local ring at $b$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_b$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{U_L,b}=\varprojlim_r\mathcal O_{U_L,b}/\mathfrak m_b^r$ for its completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], an $L$-algebra through the projection to $\operatorname{Spec}L$. Then there is a unique homomorphism of $L$-algebras $\theta:L[[T_1,\ldots,T_n]]\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{U_L,b}$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] such that, for every $r\ge1$, the image of $\theta(\sum_Ea_ET^E)$ in $\mathcal O_{U_L,b}/\mathfrak m_b^r$ is the class of the finite sum $\sum_{|E|<r}a_E\prod_i(t_i-c_i)^{e_i}$; and $\theta$ is an isomorphism of local rings, carrying $(T_1,\ldots,T_n)$ onto the maximal ideal of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{U_L,b}$ and inducing the identity of residue fields $L$. In particular $\theta(T_i)=t_i-c_i$. For $n=0$ the statement says that $L\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{U_L,b}$ (and $L\to\mathcal O_{U_L,b}$) is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 039M (lemma-characterize-etale-completions) and the remark following it (the rank n of the completion is the residue degree, so the completed map is an isomorphism when the residue extension is trivial), applied to the base change U_L -> A^n_L of the etale chart at the L-rational point b over the L-rational point (c_1,...,c_n); the completion of L[T_1,...,T_n] at (T_1-c_1,...,T_n-c_n) is the power series ring L[[T_1-c_1,...,T_n-c_n]].

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-etale-chart-rational-point-finite-jets] to the given chart and point. It supplies Noetherianity of the actual stalk B, equality I B=m_B for the centered polynomial map f, and quotient isomorphisms P/I^r = B/m_B^r with their formulas on representatives. Identify these isomorphisms with Ideal.quotientMap by quotient induction; Ideal.map_pow then gives the hypothesis of the completion-comparison theorem.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-completion-data] to f and I. Rewrite I B=m_B. Compose the resulting completion equivalence with Mathlib MvPowerSeries.toAdicCompletionAlgEquiv (Fin n) L, which identifies power series with the variables-adic completion of polynomials. Its truncation formula and the representative formula of the completion comparison give the asserted finite-level Taylor formula. Its polynomial formula gives the scalar and variable images.

Any other expansion agrees in every positive quotient, and the level-zero quotient is a zero ring. AdicCompletion.ext_evalₐ gives equality. Bijectivity is composition of the two equivalences. A surjective ring map from a local ring is local. The variables span the kernel of constant coefficient by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-kernels]; over a field this is precisely the maximal ideal, by the power-series unit criterion. Surjectivity sends it to the completion maximal ideal, whose local-ring structure follows from [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring].

Truncation at level one is the constant polynomial, proving the residue normalization. If n=0, MvPowerSeries.isEmptyEquiv identifies the series ring with L, so the completed structural scalar map is bijective. The original scalar map is injective since its source is a field. For a in B, surjectivity of the completed scalar map gives c in L with the same completion image as a. The completion map is injective by Krull separation for Noetherian local rings; hence iota(c)=a.
